title: Per-model quant defaults: confidence bands, fallback chains, and CI gating
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Establish per-model default quantization profiles in the model catalog that include recommended profile, conservative confidence bands, explicit fallback chains (FP8 -> mixed INT8 -> FP16), and CI gating rules to prevent regression in quality or safety. This ticket covers design, CI integration, validation datasets, and rollout automation for catalog entries.
background: We currently ship model variants (FP16, unquantized) and have ad hoc quant tuning notes scattered in PRs. Customers want a single per-model 'recommended quant profile' that: 1) reduces cost by at least ~25% for common workloads, 2) exposes expected accuracy variance as a confidence band, and 3) provides automatic fallback when deployed workloads exceed guardrails. Previous efforts focused on quant presets and calibration harnesses but lacked end-to-end catalog integration and CI-enforced signatures.
proposal:
Add a structured per-model quant_defaults entry in the model catalog with these fields (represented here as human-readable spec for engineering implementation):
- recommended_profile: preferred quant mode (e.g., fp8_e4m3, int8_perchannel_mixed)
- confidence_band: expected output metric variance (e.g., +-1.2% top-1 token overlap, +/-.02 perplexity)
- acceptable_regressions: numeric thresholds (perplexity_delta, task_metric_drop_pct, safety_flag_rate_change)
- fallback_chain: ordered list of fallbacks (fp8 -> int8_mixed -> fp16) with per-step rollout/percentage limits
- calibration_artifact: link to calibration dataset & calibration parameters used to derive defaults
- signature_hash: quant-signature used by CI to gate deploys
We will implement catalog schema changes, a calibration runbook, a validation CI job, and a runtime enforcement hook that can trigger automatic fallback when live traffic exceeds guardrails.
calibration_workflow:
1) Collect representative calibration corpus: 10k-50k sequences stratified by token length and request type (chat vs. single-turn completion).
2) Preprocess (tokenization, normalization) and partition: 80/10/10 (calibration/train/holdout).
3) Generate layer-wise activation statistics under FP16 baseline.
4) Run automated quant sweeps: FP8 configs (e4m3/e5m2), int8 symmetric/asymmetric per-channel, and mixed layer schemes.
5) For each candidate profile produce: token-level KL, per-layer MSE, perplexity on holdout, end-task metric delta (where available), and sample generation overlap.
6) Choose recommended_profile balancing cost reduction vs. accuracy drop and produce confidence_band by bootstrapping (N=50 resamples) on holdout.
7) Produce calibration_artifact bundle (statistics, tuning params, sample outputs) and upload to the model catalog entry.
8) Document any layer exemptions (layers pinned to FP16) and suggested per-model kernel flags.
Notes: use mocked/isolated serving environment that matches production runtime kernels to avoid mismatch between calibration and runtime behavior.
validation_plan:
- Offline checks: holdout perplexity delta <= 2% (absolute), top-1 token overlap >= 98% on general-purpose LLMs, task-specific metric drop <= 1.5% for retrieval/QA/eval prompts.
- Safety checks: no increase in safety-flagged responses above 0.5% absolute or 2x relative (whichever smaller).
- Human review: random sample of 200 generated outputs for high-risk models (customer-facing assistant).
- Regression tests: run existing eval harness (smoke, long-context, edge-case prompts) and compare to baseline signatures.
- CI gating: quant-signature job must pass (signature includes model hash, quant profile id, metrics summary). If any threshold violated, CI fails and blocks catalog merge.
- Canary rollout: enable recommended_profile on 1% traffic for 48 hours with enhanced telemetry; metrics must remain within confidence_band. If not, automatic rollback to next fallback in chain.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Schema + db migrations to support quant_defaults (feature flagged).
Phase 1: Implement calibration runner and upload hook; run for top 40 models and author catalog entries.
Phase 2: Integrate CI gating into model onboarding PRs; require quant-signature artifact for merges touching model catalog defaults.
Phase 3: Runtime enforcement: runtime accepts quant-profile tag and fallback_chain; implement automatic fallback on per-request or per-route thresholds.
Phase 4: Expand to user-requested custom profiles and UI in Console to view confidence bands and opt-out.
Owners: Modeling/Inference (Mateo), Platform (Lena Park), QA (Ravi Shah), Product (Eleanor Q.).
acceptance_criteria: catalog schema migrated behind FF and compatible with existing catalog readers
calibration runner executes end-to-end and produces calibration_artifact for a sample model
CI quant-signature job implemented and blocks merges that exceed thresholds
runtime can accept quant-profile tag and trigger fallback_chain automatically
for at least 10 widely used models, recommended_profile provides >=25% token cost reduction without violating validation thresholds
